title: A Model of Diverse Sampling from Language Models
topic: Probabilistic Methods->Monte Carlo and Sampling Methods
claim: Sets of diverse, high-quality items span a large volume under a determinantal measure, while near-duplicates from one cluster collapse to near-zero volume.
layout: 1 panel, 3D scatter with colored clusters, highlighted parallelepiped spanned by three vectors
description: A single 3D perspective scatter plot of sorting-algorithm implementations, each shown as a translucent colored dot labeled with a variant name such as random_pivot, cocktail, binary, timsort or iterative. Colors mark algorithm families: Quicksort in green, Bubble in purple, Selection in brown, Heapsort in yellow, Insertion in orange-red and Merge in blue. Family names appear as bold colored labels near their clusters. Three highlighted points, one each from Quicksort, Merge and Insertion, are ringed. Thick colored arrows run from the origin to these points and span a gray translucent parallelepiped. The box is the main visual weight and shows the spanned volume. Thin black axes and a faint grid floor frame the space. The eye goes first to the large gray box and the three bright arrows.
caption: Diverse implementations of sorting. Each point is a sorting-algorithm implementation, embedded by a code language model and projected to 3D with PCA; colors denote algorithm family. The 3- DPP assigns subset probability proportional to the squared volume of the parallelepiped spanned by the selected quality-scaled embeddings—large when the selected items are individually high-quality (large norms) and mutually dissimilar. The highlighted triple has high probability because it combines implementations from distinct algorithmic strategies, yielding a large spanned volume; by contrast, choosing three variants from the same cluster (e.g., three quicksorts) produces nearly parallel embeddings and thus near-zero volume despite high individual quality.
abstract: Language models often produce high-quality individual samples but poor sets, with repeated samples clustering around the same semantic modes. We formalize diverse generation as sampling a size-$K$ subset of complete strings from a determinantal point process (DPP), where the likelihood encodes item quality, and the embedding geometry encodes repulsion between similar outputs. Exact inference over all strings is intractable, so we propose PoolDPP: draw a finite candidate pool from a tractable proposal, importance-weight the candidates toward the target quality, and run a $K$-DPP sampler on the induced pool kernel; a greedy MAP variant provides deterministic selection. We prove a finite-sample bound with an explicit constant: the KL divergence between the sampler's output and the target $K$-DPP decays as O(1/N) in the pool size. Empirically, PoolDPP extends the quality--diversity frontier on open-ended generation and the precision--recall frontier on ambiguous text-to-SQL (Ambrosia), and on mathematical reasoning (GSM8K), it raises diversity at about the same pass@$K$.
